description: The problem requires understanding why something is happening before deciding what to do about it. The structural question is whether the proposed intervention targets the root cause or merely a symptom.
detect_when: The answer proposes a fix or intervention without establishing what caused the problem
Multiple causes could explain the same symptom — the causal hypothesis is not tested
The problem is recurring, suggesting the root cause hasn't been identified or addressed
A proximate cause is being treated as the root cause without tracing the causal chain
coverage_signals: The answer distinguishes symptoms from causes — it names the mechanism, not just the observation
The answer tests competing causal hypotheses rather than jumping to the most available explanation
The answer traces the causal chain to an actionable root — deep enough to intervene effectively
The answer considers systemic factors and feedback loops that reproduce the problem
materiality_test: Would a different causal diagnosis lead to a different intervention?
reasoning_demanded: causal reasoning, diagnostic analysis, hypothesis testing, root-cause tracing
curation_note: Root-cause-analysis provides the systematic framework for tracing symptoms to causes. Five-whys-method provides the iterative depth tool for causal chains. Correlation-vs-causation separates co-occurrence from causation. Causal-attribution-resistance addresses the cognitive resistance to accepting accurate causal explanations when they are uncomfortable. Systems-thinking addresses the systemic feedback loops that reproduce problems. Note: correlation-vs-causation also appears in information-quality — there it tests evidence quality; here it tests causal reasoning. Different structural purposes.

detect_when.note: Detection conditions from root-cause-analysis (fix without diagnosis), five-whys-method (proximate vs root cause), causal-attribution-resistance (jumping to available explanation), systems-thinking (recurring problems from unaddressed structural causes).

coverage_signals.note: Symptom vs cause distinction from root-cause-analysis. Competing hypotheses from correlation-vs-causation. Causal chain depth from five-whys-method. Systemic factors from systems-thinking.

models.note: Five models — tight coherence. Correlation-vs-causation cross-listed with information-quality: acceptable overlap because the structural purpose differs (evidence quality vs causal reasoning).
